symptom: `create or modify microflow M.F () begin @excluded declare $Variable Boolean = false; return; end;` reports success but the activity is written enabled (ActionActivity Disabled=false); DESCRIBE prints no @excluded, so the round trip of any microflow with a disabled activity re-enables it. Same for every action statement (log, call, change, ...)
cause: `flowBuilder.mergeStatementAnnotations` copies ast.ActivityAnnotations into fb.pendingAnnotations field by field and never copied `Excluded`. The visitor set it, applyAnnotations honoured it (activity.Disabled = true), the backend writes Disabled, the describer emits @excluded — every layer was right except the hand-written merge between them
insight: **Bisect by layer with the cheapest probe at each**: a visitor probe showed the AST carried Annotations, `bson dump` showed Disabled=false on disk, so the loss was between AST and write — and grepping `Disabled` showed exactly one setter, which was fine, pointing at its input. A field-by-field copy of a struct is a silent-drop site for every field added after it was written; the guard is a reflection test that sets every field and asserts it survives, with an explicit allowlist (Start, Invalid*, UnknownNames) for fields consumed elsewhere. Do not chase the backend or describer — both were already correct
